report:
**Conclusion: The evidence supports "no" — ginkgo biloba extract does not reliably relieve tinnitus symptoms.**

The most authoritative source is the Cochrane systematic review (2022), which pooled four trials (1,543 participants) and found no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity, loudness, or associated distress compared with placebo; certainty of evidence was rated low to very low across outcomes (https://www.cochrane.org/hr/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36383762/).

This aligns with an independent randomized, placebo-controlled trial and accompanying meta-analysis explicitly titled "Ginkgo biloba does not benefit patients with tinnitus," which found no significant difference versus placebo across multiple validated tinnitus outcome measures (referenced in the updated literature review: https://www.tinnitusjournal.com/articles/ginkgo-biloba-in-the-treatment-of-tinnitus-an-updated-literature-review.html).

Real-world prescription data reinforce this: a large electronic health record analysis found that patients prescribed ginkgo biloba extract for acute tinnitus were not less likely to develop chronic tinnitus compared to those not prescribed it, suggesting no protective clinical benefit in routine practice (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11323687/).

It's worth noting that the literature isn't perfectly uniform — some smaller or industry-associated studies using the specific standardized extract EGb 761® (often in combination with infusion therapy or compared to pentoxifylline) report modest subjective improvements, and some older systematic reviews argued EGb 761® specifically has "evidence-based" support. However, these positive studies tend to be smaller, less rigorously blinded, or funded by ginkgo manufacturers, whereas the largest, most rigorous, and most recent independent trials and the Cochrane review consistently show no meaningful benefit over placebo.

**Bottom line:** Major independent evidence (Cochrane, large RCTs, and real-world data) supports that ginkgo does not meaningfully relieve tinnitus, despite some conflicting smaller/industry studies.
